candidates.title: Released Dave clocks (COMMITMENT_BUDGET 120 min, log2step [38,0]) are sized for average uarch density; a guest running sfence.vma/fdiv.d-dense code makes the honest level-1 commitment take 3-8+ hours, so the honest claim can lose by timeout (A7)
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 released constants: prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol (LEVELS, log2step, height, COMMITMENT_BUDGET), ClockBudgets.sol, script/Deployment.s.sol; cost side: collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes / the uarch (honest operator)
candidates.role: Referee model, as the deployed referee (AUDIT.md: Dave released constants). The cost being under-provisioned is that of the honest operator's uarch-level claim builder (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, honest operator role).
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol (COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 minutes; log2step = [38,0]; height = [54,38]); ClockBudgets.sol (refill = commitmentBudget + 2*responseBudget; maxAllowance = censorship + 2*response + (levels-1)*refill); Tournament.sol sealInnerMatch -> pauseForInnerAt/instantiateInner (child allowance = remaining clock) and winInnerTournament (refill only on return); derivation documented in docs/measurements/constants.md and docs/dimensioning.md ('Coordinates are dimensioned to the worst case. Clocks are dimensioned to the average case.')
candidates.description: With the released geometry a level-0 leaf is 2^38 meta-cycles = 2^18 mcycles, so when a level-0 match is sealed the honest operator must build a level-1 commitment of height 38 over 2^18 mcycles, i.e. run the uarch with a state hash after every uarch cycle for 2^18 mcycles (one bundle root per mcycle). The only time the clocks reserve for that build is COMMITMENT_BUDGET = 120 min (plus two 5-minute inclusions); the rest of the allowance is the censorship budget. Dave derived this budget from a measured leaf-build rate of 173 big cycles/s at an AVERAGE density of 566 usteps per mcycle (constants.md, 'clocks price the trusted app's AVERAGE density'), explicitly not the worst instruction mix (dimensioning.md calls a dense sqrt/TLB-flush region an 'un-disputable machine' excluded by a trusted-app assumption). The threat model has no such assumption: A7 requires clocks 'at the worst-case costs of R12', the guest is fully adversarial after it reads an input (section 4), and a correctly designed application only bounds its mcycle count, not the uarch density of its mcycles. Measured on audit/prt2: sfence.vma costs 17,056 usteps per mcycle (31x Dave's density label) and fdiv.d 4,564 (8x); hashed uarch collection (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, bundle 2^20, as the PRT player builds uarch claims) runs 19.7x and 7.3x slower than an add loop (545 usteps/mcycle, i.e. Dave's density) on the same host. Scaled to Dave's own reference rate (173/s), a 2^18-mcycle level-1 commitment over such code takes ~29,800 s (8.3 h) for sfence.vma and ~11,000 s (3.1 h) for fdiv.d, versus 120 min, before Dave's own hardware-slack factor 2 (16.6 h / 6.1 h).
candidates.trigger: Adversary (input sender + dishonest claimant): sends an input that takes control of the guest (section 4) and runs a loop of sfence.vma (or fdiv.d/fsqrt.d) for at least 2^18 mcycles while staying within the application's mcycle bound - or simply targets an application whose legitimate input-driven code is FP- or TLB-flush-dense in some 2^18-mcycle window (e.g. a user process looping on mprotect/munmap, each causing kernel sfence.vma). It then posts a level-0 claim that diverges from the honest one inside that window, steers the bisection there (section 7: 'Steer the dispute to any position'), seals the match, and joins the inner tournament immediately with any commitment (a fabricated one costs nothing). It censors the honest operator's transactions within the censorship budget (allowed: the adversary is only 'not assumed to ... censor the chain beyond the dispute clocks'); on a DEVNET deployment (censorship budget 0) no censorship is needed at all.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: any guest can execute sfence.vma in S/M mode or fdiv.d with FS enabled (bare-metal M-mode loops measured below; under Linux, a kernel controlled by the input, or user code doing FP math / repeated mprotect). No unreachable state is involved; the cost is the specified uarch semantics, linear per R12, only the sizing is wrong.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is a guest instruction mix plus adversary capabilities of section 7. 'Defects that need the deployment to violate one of A1 to A8' are excluded 'unless ... an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)'; AUDIT.md makes Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 with its RELEASED constants the referee model as the deployed referee, so its A7 violation is in scope. Not 'average-case performance' (this is the worst case), not an application loss ('The honest operator still defends the trajectory the state transition function defines, for any application').

2. Role: referee model (Dave released constants). Section 3: 'Which claim a timeout or an elimination decides is part of what it derives.' A competing reading: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond ... is rated as support' -> support standing in for the deployed referee -> Medium. The deciding fact is whether an under-sized commitment budget is 'only how long a claim may take to respond' or a clock rule that eliminates the honest claim; A7 says 'No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock', which points to the former reading being too narrow.

3. High/Medium cases: the High case 'A defect that lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor ... while staying within what the deployment was sized for' does not fit: the deployment is NOT sized for it, and the cost is 'A cost that the specified semantics require'.

4. Critical: A7 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim to play the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces on it, at the worst-case costs of R12' is violated: the worst-case cost of 'a uarch-level claim' (R12) over one released level-0 leaf exceeds COMMITMENT_BUDGET by 1.5x-8x at Dave's own reference rate. Section 8 Critical: 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make ... larger than what the deployment was sized for.' Goal threat: completeness failure ('The honest operator ... cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win').
5. Not Low. Claimed: Critical (Medium under the 'support: response time only' reading of section 3).
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness: the honest claim cannot join the inner tournament (or cannot finish its level-1 commitment) before its clock runs out; the dishonest commitment wins the inner tournament alone and, per A1, its last leaf decides the enclosing match, eliminating the honest claim; with no honest claim left any claim can settle, including a fabricated final state and outputs.
candidates.evidence: Scratch /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERDEPLOY: guests g/*.S built with bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh (sfence.S: 32x sfence.vma + j; fdivun.S: 32x fdiv.d + j; add.S baseline), measured with measure-density.lua (64 MiB RAM image, run 16 mcycles, then run_uarch/reset_uarch per mcycle to count usteps, then time collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes(mcycle+K, 20, tail)). Results on this shared 4-CPU host (load ~10, absolute times inflated, ratios meaningful): add 545-548 usteps/mcycle, 70.9-89.7 mcycles/s; fdiv.d (unrolled) 4,564 usteps/mcycle, 12.3 mcycles/s; fsqrt.d ~3,800 per instruction; sfence.vma 17,056 usteps/mcycle, 3.6 mcycles/s; divu 612, mulhu 852, fmadd.d 993 (with loop overhead). Dave's constants.md: 173 big cycles/s at 566 usteps; its 60-minute derivation already uses [38,0]/[54,38] and the deployed 120 min is 'double slack'. Dave's own dimensioning.md acknowledges: 'code built from instructions whose uarch emulation is maximally long (the sqrt / TLB-flush class), dense enough that building a nested commitment over any gap of it exceeds any realistic timeout. Nothing currently detects these.'
candidates.test_idea: Deterministic sizing test (no wall clock needed beyond a calibration): build the sfence.vma bare-metal loop, count usteps per mcycle with run_uarch over N mcycles (deterministic: 17,056 mean), compute worst-case usteps for one released level-0 leaf (2^(log2step(0)-20) mcycles x usteps) and compare with the ustep budget implied by Dave's own derivation (COMMITMENT_BUDGET seconds x 84,522 usteps+hash/s / hardware slack, or 173 big cycles/s x 566 usteps x 7200 s); assert worst-case <= budget. It fails by ~8x-30x. Alternatively an end-to-end test on the local chain with a DEVNET-style deployment and the released geometry, a guest looping on sfence.vma, and a dishonest player that seals into that leaf; assert the honest claim wins.

candidates.title: machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 cannot be regenerated from audit/prt2: UArchStep.sol references TLB_NUM_SETS, which the constants generator never emits (TLB constants are hand-copied in the template), so the referee verifier is not reproducibly buildable from audited source (R13)
candidates.component: machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 generator (helper_scripts/generate_UArchStep.sh, helper_scripts/generate_EmulatorConstants.lua, templates/EmulatorConstants.sol.template) together with src/uarch-step.cpp of audit/prt2
candidates.location: src/uarch-step.cpp:890 ('if (set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS || slot_index >= TLB_SET_SIZE)', added by afd5f9d); solidity-step templates/EmulatorConstants.sol.template lines 28-30 (hand-written TLB_SLOT_LENGTH = 32, TLB_SET_SIZE = 256, TLB_SET_LENGTH; no TLB_NUM_SETS); helper_scripts/generate_EmulatorConstants.lua (emits no TLB_* sizes although cartesi.TLB_NUM_SETS / cartesi.TLB_SET_SIZE exist, src/clua-cartesi.cpp:337-338); generate_UArchStep.sh qualifies only identifiers found in EmulatorConstants.sol
candidates.description: The deployment's verifier is defined as machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 with its generated code and constants regenerated from audit/prt2. Running the project's own generate-step against audit/prt2 translates the new WRITE_TLB bound check into 'set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS' left unqualified (the translator only prefixes names that EmulatorConstants.sol declares), and EmulatorConstants.sol (template + generator) declares no TLB_NUM_SETS, so 'forge build' fails with 'Undeclared identifier'. A deployment engineer therefore cannot rebuild the verifier from audited source; the only way to deploy is a hand edit (the harness adds 'uint64 constant TLB_NUM_SETS = 3;' to the template), i.e. unaudited source with a third hand-copied TLB constant. The other TLB sizes the verifier uses to compute shadow-TLB addresses (TLB_SET_SIZE, TLB_SLOT_LENGTH) are also hand-copied rather than generated from the emulator, so a future change of the emulator's TLB geometry would regenerate silently with stale values.
candidates.trigger: Deployment engineer regenerating the verifier from audit/prt2 with the step's documented targets (generate-step generate-reset generate-send-cmio-response generate-constants generate-prod).
candidates.reachability: Deterministic: every regeneration from audit/prt2 fails. (The semantic effect of a wrong hand-chosen TLB_NUM_SETS would only show from unreachable before-states, since the pristine uarch never issues an out-of-range WRITE_TLB.)
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No: R13 requires 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source'; this is about the verifier build, not a deployment obligation violation.

2. Role: referee verifier (AUDIT.md: machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1 with generated code regenerated from audit/prt2). The defect is the interface between the emulator source and the step generator; whichever side is fixed, the verifier is what cannot be built.

3. High case matches: 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' (If a deployer hand-patches it, what is deployed no longer matches audited source, which would move it toward Critical under R13/A6.)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The goal relies on the on-chain verifier implementing the same transition function as the honest operator (A6, R13). If the verifier cannot be regenerated from the audited emulator, deployers hand-patch generated code or deploy a stale verifier; nobody can check that the on-chain bytecode corresponds to the audited transition function.
candidates.evidence: Reproduced in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERDEPLOY/step: copied released helper_scripts/templates and src/EmulatorConstants.sol/EmulatorCompat.sol, ran EMULATOR_DIR=/home/user/machine-emulator ./helper_scripts/generate_UArchStep.sh: src/UArchStep.sol line 780 'if (set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS || slot_index >= EmulatorConstants.TLB_SET_SIZE)', and grep finds no 'constant TLB_NUM_SETS' in EmulatorConstants.sol. The harness's full regeneration (bugs/harness/work/solidity-step/build-status.txt) records 'forge build FAILED: Error (7576): Undeclared identifier ... src/UArchStep.sol:1090:30 set_index >= TLB_NUM_SETS'. Constants regenerated with the in-tree Lua module match the harness's regenerated constants; UArchReset/SendCmioResponse regenerate unchanged (modulo forge fmt).
candidates.test_idea: Script: clone/copy machine-solidity-step v0.17.0-test1, run generate-step/reset/send-cmio-response/constants/prod with EMULATOR_DIR=audit/prt2, run 'forge build'; assert exit 0 and that every identifier of src/uarch-step.cpp used in UArchStep.sol is either declared or generated (no unqualified constant). Also assert the TLB_* values in EmulatorConstants.sol equal cartesi.TLB_NUM_SETS/TLB_SET_SIZE and the shadow slot size.

candidates.title: The uarch toolchain is only partly pinned: binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf and libc6-dev-riscv64-cross float with the live Debian archive, so the pristine uarch binary and hash are not reproducibly rebuildable over time (R13)
candidates.component: Dockerfile (toolchain stage) and uarch/Makefile (uarch program build)
candidates.role: Honest operator (uarch program and its pristine hash, fixed on-chain via UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH)
candidates.location: Dockerfile lines 4-16: debian:trixie-20250811 with apt-get from the live archive; only g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu=14.2.0-19cross1 and gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf=14.2.0+19 pinned. uarch/Makefile: CC/CXX/LD/OBJCOPY = riscv64-unknown-elf-* (assembler/linker from binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, unpinned, currently 2.44-3+7+b1), TOOLCHAIN_INCS = /usr/riscv64-linux-gnu/include (libc6-dev-riscv64-cross, unpinned, currently 2.41-11cross1), objcopy -O binary produces uarch-ram.bin whose hash is the pristine hash.
candidates.description: uarch-ram.bin (and so UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH, which a deployment fixes on-chain and the honest player compares) is produced by riscv64-unknown-elf-as/ld/objcopy and compiled against cross glibc headers that the Dockerfile does not pin, installed from deb.debian.org (not snapshot.debian.org). Assembler/linker relaxation, alignment padding and section layout depend on binutils; Debian stable rebuilds (binNMUs such as '+b1') and point releases replace these packages, and the live archive also drops superseded versions, so the two pinned packages themselves become uninstallable after a point release replaces them. A deployment engineer rebuilding later from the same commit either cannot build the toolchain image or may obtain a different uarch-ram.bin and pristine hash.
candidates.trigger: Deployment engineer (or auditor) rebuilding the uarch from audited source after the Debian trixie archive moves (point release or binNMU of binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, libc6-dev-riscv64-cross, or the pinned gcc packages).
candidates.reachability: Latent: today the harness rebuild reproduces 0x89ae34ba...43d7 bit-for-bit. Failure depends on archive changes outside the repository.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No; R13: 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source.'
2. Role: honest operator (uarch program, per AUDIT.md component table).

3. High case: 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' Fits once the archive moves; today it rebuilds, so a strict reading gives Low ('a real defect that violates no rule' yet). Deciding fact: whether R13's 'reproducibly buildable' covers the build inputs being pinned, or only that a rebuild matches today.
candidates.threat_to_goal: If the pristine uarch cannot be rebuilt, nobody can confirm that the hash fixed on-chain comes from the audited interpreter (A6/R13); a re-deployment from source could produce a different pristine hash than the one existing templates and verifiers carry, splitting the deployment version.
candidates.evidence: docker run cartesi/machine-emulator:toolchain dpkg -l: binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf 2.44-3+7+b1, libc6-dev-riscv64-cross 2.41-11cross1 (both unpinned in the Dockerfile), gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf 14.2.0+19 and g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu 14.2.0-19cross1 (pinned). Harness report work/uarch-rebuild/report.txt notes binutils is not pinned; current rebuild matches.
candidates.test_idea: Static test: parse the Dockerfile and assert that every package that provides a tool or header used by uarch/Makefile (riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,g++,as,ld,objcopy}, /usr/riscv64-linux-gnu/include) is pinned to an exact version and that apt sources point at a snapshot (snapshot.debian.org) matching the base image date. Dynamic: rebuild the uarch with binutils from a different Debian version and compare uarch-ram.bin.

candidates.title: The PRT player's deployment check covers only UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH: it never compares the deployed CM_MARCHID, and nothing published by the verifier identifies its generated step/reset/cmio code, so a verifier whose code and constants come from different emulator versions passes every check (R13)
candidates.component: doc/recipes/crisium.lua (startup checks), doc/recipes/prt-deploy.lua; machine-solidity-step build (generate-constants vs generate-step inputs); CartesiStateTransition published constants
candidates.role: Support (PRT player and deploy recipe; AUDIT.md: 'No production deployment runs the player'). The underlying gap (no published identity of the verifier code) concerns the referee verifier.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/crisium.lua:128-132 (only UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH() compared); prt-deploy.lua:44-47 (same); doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua:873-893 read_geometry (factory heights vs emulator ROLLUP_* constants, but the STF's own ROLLUP_* constants, DaveConsensus MAX_INPUTS_PER_EPOCH and CM_MARCHID are never read); Dave CartesiStateTransition publishes CM_MARCHID and UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH, both produced by generate-constants, while UArchStep/UArchReset/SendCmioResponse come from generate-step etc. against EMULATOR_DIR sources.
candidates.description: R13 requires that 'The honest operator must be able to detect and refuse a mismatch between its build and a deployment.' The pristine uarch hash only identifies the uarch RAM image (the main interpreter compiled for the uarch). It does not change with changes to src/uarch-step.cpp, uarch-reset-state.cpp, send-cmio-response.cpp (e.g. the halt/overflow precedence and WRITE_TLB bound check that distinguish audit/prt2 from v0.17.0-test1's UArchStep.sol), the dispute constants, or the hash-tree construction. The recipe player does not even compare the deployed CM_MARCHID with cartesi.MARCHID, and CM_MARCHID itself is emitted by generate-constants, not by the code generators, so a verifier built with fresh constants and stale generated code (or vice versa) publishes matching identification. Also note: audit/prt2 identifies itself as CM_VERSION '0.23.0-test2' / mimpid 23, the same as the already released upstream v0.23.0-test2 (marchid 22, different transition function); only marchid separates them.
candidates.trigger: Deployment engineer honest mistake: regenerates constants but not the step code (or regenerates against a different checkout), or deploys Dave with a step whose ROLLUP_* constants differ from the emulator's; honest operator starts crisium against it.
candidates.reachability: For today's released versions every concrete pairing I found is refused by the pristine-hash or template-hash checks, and the code differences between released v0.17.0-test1 UArchStep.sol and the audit/prt2 regeneration matter only from unreachable before-states (uarch halting exactly on its last cycle; WRITE_TLB with set >= 3). So the gap has no reachable effect today.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Mixed versions violate A6 (a deployment obligation), but R13 places the detection duty on the honest operator ('The check must refuse every pairing of its build with a deployment of another released version'), so the detection gap itself is in scope.
2. Role: support (PRT player/deploy recipe). A defect only a support component shows is at most Medium.

3. High case 'A node that cannot detect a version mismatch, while every node in fact runs the deployment's version' would apply to a production node; for the player it maps to Medium only if the pairing involves another released version, which I could not exhibit (released v0.22.0, v0.23.0-test1, v0.23.0-test2 share the old pristine hash, and audit/prt2's differs).
5. Low: no concrete released pairing is accepted; the gap is structural (identification does not cover the verifier code).
candidates.threat_to_goal: If a future release changes only host-side uarch semantics or dispute constants, the honest operator's only check (pristine hash) would accept a deployment of the other version, and honest proofs could fail or a wrong proof be accepted at the changed boundary (A6).
candidates.evidence: Read crisium.lua/prt-deploy.lua checks; compared released step v0.16.0 (Dave pin fb00a32) and v0.17.0-test1 (identical generated files and constants: marchid 22, 0x558f...3926); fetched upstream tag Makefiles: v0.22.0 (marchid 22, minor 22), v0.23.0-test1 (marchid 22, minor 22, label ''), v0.23.0-test2 (marchid 22, minor 23, label -test2), audit/prt2 (marchid 23, minor 23, label -test2); STF sources unchanged between those three releases.
candidates.test_idea: Deploy the released Dave build with a CartesiStateTransition whose step code is v0.17.0-test1's UArchStep.sol but constants regenerated from audit/prt2; start crisium; assert it refuses the deployment (today it accepts). Or a unit test of the player's startup checks asserting it reads and compares CM_MARCHID and a code identity of the verifier.

not_covered: Did not run forge build/tests or deploy anything myself; relied on the harness's regenerated-patched build and results for compile/test status (I re-ran only the step/reset/cmio translators and the constants generator with the in-tree Lua module).
Did not verify the absolute leaf-build rate on validator-grade hardware; my timings are on a loaded shared 4-CPU host and are used only as ratios against Dave's published 173 big cycles/s.

Did not search exhaustively for the worst uarch-density instruction (only add, divu, mulhu, fmadd.d, fdiv.d, fsqrt.d, subnormal variants, sfence.vma); page walks with many PMAs/Sv57 and trap-heavy sequences may be worse.
Did not check the root (level-0) clock sizing: worst-case cost of reaching a disputed period from the nearest snapshot and root slowdown at worst-case density.

Did not compare Dave's computation-hash construction (padding, leaf placement) against the emulator's collect_* builders beyond the geometry constants.
Did not check the machine-guest-tools release for constants duplicated with the emulator (rx/tx buffer sizes, yield reasons).
